title: The version status, the effective dates, the approver reference, the four matrix operations and the right of the load are not specified for the permission matrix
description: (a) `permission` carries `matrix_version` (DF-REF-044) and the standard `state` column of TSD P4 v3 T3.0, and no valid-from date, valid-to date or approver reference, while legacy AC3 needs an approved version with a valid from date and the story needs the status LOADED, VALIDATED, APPROVED and IN_FORCE; (b) the matrix load, the matrix read, the version read and the versions list have no row in the ownership map and none in TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A, whose only role read is GET /admin/roles (API-P4-007) and whose reference-load paths (API-P4-005, API-P4-006, API-P4-009 and API-P4-010) are P3 rwb-case's under ASM-A6-api-4 with the approval in RWB-P4-AD010-APP; (c) the legacy Permission checks table gives the load the C letter of Reference data for RW-COE and RW-REFADM and the approval the A letter of Rules and parameters for RW-RISK, while TSD P4 v3 T6.1 puts the permission rows in Platform administration (RW-SECADM CRUDA, RW-PLATADM CRUD, RW-AUDIT R) and gives RW-REFADM no right there; (d) the legacy criterion names the application owner's approval and TSD P4 v3 T6.1 holds no application-owner role and no approval right for the `permission` table, so the approver of a matrix version is unfixed; (e) the number of roles a complete matrix must cover is not stated (TSD P4 v3 T6.1 lists 42 role codes while the legacy criteria of the same matrix count 54 roles and 756 rows); (f) where the load form of the matrix sits on a screen is not stated, and the legacy screens SCR-39 and SCR-40 belong to the rule-version and reference-list stories.
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-002); Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3 (T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T6.1, appendix T-A.1); Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3 (A2.4, AC-EXC-P4-004-02, Screens); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 (slides 14, 20, 41 and 43); Ownership Map v1
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 permission (DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044, no date column) and T3.0 standard record columns (state); TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A.1 (API-P4-005 to API-P4-010 reference loads, API-P4-007 roles only); legacy RWB-AD-002 Endpoints and Permission checks tables; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (RW-SECADM CRUDA, RW-PLATADM CRUD, RW-REFADM CRUD in Reference data only); FSD P4 v3 A2.4 field catalog (permission.letters C, R, U, D and A or a dash; capability area one of the 14) and AC-P4-004-01 (756 rows); ownership map rulings ASM-A6-api-3 and ASM-A6-api-4
area: Access and role administration; API contract
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-access with the security administrator and the application owner
proposed: Hold the version label in `permission.matrix_version`, the status in the standard `state` column and the valid-from, valid-to and approver-reference columns this key adds by its own migration; fix the four operations under `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/permission-matrix` with Platform administration R for the three reads and C for the load; end the load at VALIDATED and leave the approval to RWB-P4-AD010-APP with the approver role read from the parameter rwb.refload.approver.permission; compute the expected row count from `role` and LOV-CAPABILITY and never fix it in code; show the matrix and the versions on SCR-43 through the gateway-bff route and leave the screen field list to the platform story.

title: The matrix contract shapes, its four paths, its status vocabulary and its event payload are not specified
description: (a) the field names, types and lengths of the matrix row, the matrix, the version and the page, and the valid-from and valid-to dates, the approver reference and the pending approver role, have no physical definition in any source; (b) the paths, the rights, the request and answer shapes and the error responses of the four operations have no row in the ownership map and none in TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A; (c) the state of a version at the end of a load is not stated for the matrix and is taken from LOV-VERSION-STATUS (LOADED, VALIDATED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED), with no source saying whether a load ends LOADED or VALIDATED; (d) no source names the payload of an access-policy event for a matrix version, the change kind MATRIX and the decision codes AC-VERS and AC-DENY are this revision's own use of the service's existing vocabulary, and the point at which the event is published (the load, the approval, or the effective date) is not stated; (e) the legacy permission rows Reference data C and Rules and parameters A are not the rights of these operations and no source names the replacement right explicitly for the matrix; (f) the deprecation window of a published field and the retention of the contract fakes are not stated.
source: Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3 (T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T4, T6.1, appendix T-A.1); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-002); Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3 (A2.4); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 (slides 11, 14, 20, 41 and 43); Ownership Map v1
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (no version, status or date column on permission beyond matrix_version), T3.2 (LOV-VERSION-STATUS and LOV-CAPABILITY with its 14 values), T4 (the rule package version lifecycle as the nearest precedent) and appendix T-A.1 (no matrix operation); Architecture v5 slides 14, 20 and 43 (rwb.access.events.v1 carries AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged only, with the cache-refresh consumers); legacy RWB-AD-002 Data, Endpoints and Permission checks tables; ownership map (permission and role are P4's; parameters, reference data and the reference-load paths are P3's)
area: Access and role administration; API contract
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-access with the solution architect
proposed: Fix the four operations and the four schemas in the contract baseline of this key, with Platform administration R for the reads and C for the load, one problem envelope with the seven message IDs and the six fakes; declare the load as `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` with change kind MATRIX on `rwb.access.events.v1` and the entry on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; state VALIDATED as the end state of a load and APPROVED and IN_FORCE as the approval gate's; leave the field-level detail to the contract review and record the deprecation and retention decisions with the platform contract owner.
